title: Financial Analysis
overview: In the modern business environment, finance professionals must go beyond basic reporting to deliver detailed insights into the impact of organizational financial decisions. This requires expertise in deciphering financial statements, analyzing figures, interpreting ratios, and presenting data-driven recommendations effectively.

This course equips participants with the skills to understand the relationships within financial statements, perform ratio analysis, and present actionable insights. Using real-world examples from published financial statements and Excel tools, participants will learn how to turn raw data into meaningful financial analyses.
audience: This course is ideal for finance and accounting professionals, financial analysts, department heads, senior managers, financial controllers, finance managers, and chief accountants who are involved in business analysis and financial decision-making.
methodology: The course combines theoretical knowledge with practical applications of Excel to enhance financial analysis. Participants will engage in real-life case studies, dynamic exercises, and group discussions, culminating in presentations and feedback sessions.
competencies: Understanding audited financial statements and annual reports
Performing vertical and horizontal financial analyses
Conducting liquidity, efficiency, solvency, and profitability analyses
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Understand and apply the framework for financial statement analysis.
Perform financial and ratio analysis effectively.
Interpret company financials and assess industry positions.
Analyze real-life financial statements of companies listed on global and GCC stock exchanges.
Develop and utilize financial analysis template models.

items.text: Role and importance of financial reporting and analysis
Key financial statements and the significance of annual reports
Understanding the role of notes and supplementary information
Objectives and types of financial statement audits
Financial statement analysis framework and the accounting cycle
Financial reporting mechanics and the relationships within financial statements
Importance of reporting standards in financial analysis and valuation
Overview of standards-setting bodies
Comparison of IFRS and GAAP
Income Statement:
Key components, revenue, and expense recognition
Balance Sheet:
Measurement, classification, and key components
Statement of Changes in Owners’ Equity:
Structure and analysis
Cash Flow Statement:
Operating, investing, and financing activities
Direct vs. indirect preparation methods
Interpreting cash flows and understanding the "cash-rich" standard
Vertical Analysis: Strategies for balance sheets and income statements
Horizontal and Trend Analysis: Growth evaluation techniques
Liquidity Analysis: Current, quick, and cash ratios, and cash conversion cycles
Asset Management Ratios: Total and fixed asset turnover
Solvency Analysis: Debt-to-equity, times interest earned, and related ratios
Profitability Analysis: Gross margin, profit margin, ROA, and ROE
Market and Valuation Metrics: Price-to-earnings ratio and EPS
DuPont Analysis: Three-step and five-step models for in-depth financial evaluation
Recognizing the limitations of ratio analysis
Evaluating a company’s past financial performance
Conducting comprehensive analyses of publicly traded companies using real-world case studies
